newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent dips as NYMEX fails to hold small gain.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent dips as NYMEX fails to hold small gain.

text.p: Brent crude futures dipped a few cents on Thursday on very light volume as NYMEX crudes gave up modest gains, brokers said.
August Brent on SIMEX was last traded at $17.76 per barrel, down one cent from London overnight, where the contract fell 31 cents to $17.77 per barrel. Market volume was just 26 lots.
Earlier NYMEX prices on ACCESS made slight gains from New York, but by late trading in Asia had pared them back.
July NYMEX crude was last traded at $18.79, unchanged from New York and after being three cents higher earlier in the Asian day.
August was last traded at $18.97, up one cent from New York but off the earlier price of $19.01.
The London market opened a chart gap on the front-month between $18.02, the low on Tuesday and $17.98, the high of Wednesday, which brokers said on Thursday would limit the upside for now.
Brokers said they expected a delay to Iraqi crude exports to produce only modest support for the market.
News of delays failed to provide any support for a sliding London market overnight.
